## 1. Finite-depth clocks realize every finite power of omega

For each positive integer d, define a d-level survival clock by lexicographically nesting d finite counters, with the outer counters contributing successive ordinal blocks. The conjecture is that the supremum of all clock readings is exactly ω^d, while every reading remains strictly below ω^d.

The key insight is that the verified passage from finite delays to ω, and from finite block budgets with finite tails to ω², should iterate through ordinal multiplication.

Why now? The one-level and two-level cases expose the induction invariant: each new finite choice layer takes the supremum of finite right multiples of the preceding clock.

## 2. Operational infinite-time machines realize the same two-level clock

Consider an infinite-time register machine with a specified limit-stage update rule and a Mortal controller choosing finite delay bounds at successor stages. The conjecture is that there is a concrete program/game pair whose attainable halting times are cofinal in ω² and whose rank agrees with the two-parameter block clock.

There exists a finitely branching, well-founded survival tree of rank ω² such that every branch is finite, and every fixed finite branching budget determines a subtree of rank strictly below ω². If a single natural number B globally bounds the outer nondeterministic budget, then the supremum of all finite-tail plays is conjectured to be exactly ω·B + ω and therefore strictly below ω²; conversely, any family cofinal in ω² must have unbounded outer budgets.
